Our Senior Pastor teaches that good works are not the cause of salvation but rather its result and evidence [1][3]. She emphasizes that good works are an integral part of God's pre-ordained plan for every believer [4][9].

Here are six things our Senior Pastor teaches about good works:
1.  **Good works are part of God's plan.** She explains that God's plan predates our birth, both biological and spiritual. God planned for us to do certain good works even before we were born and before we were born again [4]. Just as God pre-ordained our salvation, He also pre-ordained our good works [4][16].
2.  **Good works are the proof of salvation.** They are not the price we pay to be saved, but evidence that we are saved, showing that we have the divine nature of God [1]. When we do good works like forgiving others or being generous, we prove that we are like our Father, who Himself does good works and is a giving God (John 3:16) [1].
3.  **Good works are the result of salvation, not its cause.** Under the law, people performed good works to earn salvation, acceptance, or justification. However, as new creations in Christ, we do good works because we are already justified, not to earn God's approval, but because He has already approved of us [3]. Our salvation is a gift received through grace by faith, not by works, so no one can boast (Ephesians 2:8-10) [2][9][16].
4.  **Good works are the result of God working in the believer's heart.** Our Senior Pastor teaches that people don't naturally do good. Even moralists or atheists who appear to do good often have a "what's in it for me" motive; it's an investment they expect to yield a return. A person without God's nature cannot genuinely be generous [3].
5.  **Good works are primarily the work of the ministry.** While some might misdefine "good works," our Senior Pastor clarifies that the good works God has ordained for us (Ephesians 2:10) refer primarily to the work of the ministry [2]. This includes strengthening, enlightening, encouraging, and exalting others, using the power of God for edification and not destruction (2 Corinthians 13:10) [2][18].
6.  **We are created in Christ Jesus unto good works.** God creates each of us by Christ Jesus to join Him in His work. Just as Jesus "went about doing good and healing all that were oppressed of the devil because God was with him" (Acts 10:38), we are redeemed to participate in this noble work. Our purpose and the meaning of our lives are found in Jesus, where every void is filled [9][14].

Salvation itself is a complete package (soteria), encompassing deliverance from every work of darkness, wholeness in spirit, soul, and body, and freedom from demonic oppression. This entire work of redemption was completed on the cross of Calvary; there is nothing else we need God to do that He has not already done in Christ (John 10:10) [5][6][13]. The plan of redemption was always God's plan, not an afterthought, and was prophesied thousands of years before Jesus' birth [12]. We receive this forgiveness and salvation through believing in our hearts that God raised Jesus from the dead and confessing Him with our mouths (Romans 10:9-10) [10].

Your giving profile, which includes your offerings and partnership offering, should be instructed by God, not pressured by man [14].

Dad also teaches that God increases His children through their giving; it is a kingdom principle that gives God permission to turn insufficiency into more than enough [2]. Generosity should not be selective, but should extend to all areas of life, including family and those outside the church [16].

To overcome fear and anxiety, Dad teaches that you must decisively deal with fear, as it is a spirit of bondage that can paralyze and hinder progress [3][10][16]. You can conquer fear by relying on the infallibility of God's Word, praying, and allowing God to heal your wounds [2][5][9].

Here's how Dad teaches you can overcome fear and anxiety:
*   **Decisively Deal with Fear** Dad emphasizes that fear is an enemy of a sound mind and can make people irrational [3]. It is a tormenting spirit that paralyzes, hinders, and incapacitates [10]. He likens fear to cancer, noting that it spreads, so it must be cut off immediately [12]. You must make up your mind that fear will no longer be a companion in your life's journey [3]. Any fear in your life should be dealt with, not tolerated [16].
*   **Confront and Expose Fears to God** Champions are people who overcome fears, not those who never had them [1]. God may confront you with fears that have been "dogging" you, and you must bring them out [1]. Expose any remaining fear to God, just as you would repent from sin, asking Him to deliver you from it [5]. Dad recounts a dream where he faced a fierce lion and, by rebuking it in his spirit, saw it cower like a dog and run away, signifying the end of that fear in his life [1].
*   **Pray and Let God Heal** Allow God to touch and heal your wounds rather than sweeping them under the carpet [2]. Dad shares a personal testimony of returning to the same hospital where he and our Senior Pastor had suffered miscarriages, deliberately going back to let the devil know that God had done His best and they lived without trauma or fear [2]. When you are done praying about certain things, rest your heart in God [13]. You can also repent from fear, crying out to the Lord like David did in Psalm 34, asking Him to deliver you from all fears [5][12].
*   **Rely on God's Word and Intimacy** Dad teaches that meditating on scriptures like "The Lord is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear?" (Psalm 27:1) can help knock out fears [8]. He highlights that Pastor Funlola Alabi teaches that under the ministry of God's Word, fears disappear [10]. When you rely on the infallibility of God's Word, you can believe what it says about the future, regardless of uncertainties [9]. Spending time in intimacy with God, as David did, allows Him to teach you to be fearless and face adversity head-on, leading to victory over challenges [6].
*   **Distract Yourself with Purpose and Cast Burdens on God** Every moment spent worrying is a distraction from your purpose [7]. Let your purpose in God be your distraction from anxiety; focus on it to divert your mind from worries [7]. Anxiety opens the door to the enemy [13]. Instead, cast your burden upon the Lord, and He will sustain you, ensuring you are not moved, as anxiety tends to shake people [13][17].

Key themes from these messages include:
*   **The Nature of Faith:** Faith is defined as the substance of things hoped for and the evidence of things not seen (Hebrews 11:1). Its core is the spoken word of God, which becomes alive and real when you receive it [2][8]. He cautions against marrying based solely on physical "figure," stressing that it is meaningful only after you have figured out what is important in life [6][14]. Dad teaches extensively on Romans 8:28, emphasizing that "all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose" [1].

Here's what Dad says across various messages:
*   In **Not My Purpose but His Purpose for My Life**, Dad explains that Romans 8:28 highlights God's purpose for our lives, not our own. He emphasizes that while "my purpose in life" and "God's purpose for my life" sound similar, they are "worlds apart," with God's purpose being the true scriptural focus [1].
*   In **Midweek Service**, Dad connects Romans 8:28 to the Holy Spirit's role in prayer. He teaches that when the Holy Spirit helps us pray according to God's will, that prayer, done in line with God's will, then works for our good. He clarifies that the context of "all things working together for good" is the will of God that the Holy Ghost helps to pray out [2][18].
*   In **GOD's Principle of Faithfulness 2 - Ambidextrous Believers Part 15**, Dad states that Romans 8:28 shows there is a purpose behind everything God does. He teaches that even things God did not initiate, God can take and use for His purpose. Evil, though not caused by God, can be "God used" and will be incorporated into His purpose [4][7].
*   In **Day 27 - Evening Session**, Dad reiterates that Romans 8:28 means "whatever God's hand is on will work for his purpose." He uses the example of Judas, saying that even though Judas became a betrayer, his actions still worked for Jesus's good because God had brought Judas into Jesus's life [5][16].
*   In **Prayer Works**, Dad encourages walking in God's will because then "things begin to come together for your good" as the Bible says all things work together for good [8].
*   In **Day 30**, Dad stresses that we must consider God's plan and purpose for our lives, as revealed in Romans 8:28. He reminds us that God's thoughts are of peace and not evil, to give us an expected end (Jeremiah 29:11), and that His plan for our life came out of His love for us [10][15].
*   In **Faith, Foolishness, Presumptions or Fear - Part 5**, Dad quotes Romans 8:28 as a "certain knowing" or conviction, similar to Job's conviction that his Redeemer lives, or Paul's knowledge of whom he has believed. He presents it as a truth we know for sure [13].

Dad teaches that Mark 11:23 means you must trust God with your whole life and give voice to your faith by speaking His word [2][3][4][13][14]. He emphasizes that faith is not just believing, but also acting on what you believe [3][16].

Here's how Dad elaborates on this:
*   **Trust in God** Faith is putting your absolute trust in God and His word [4][13][16]. You cannot be trusting in man, yourself, your boss, or your investments; you must trust God entirely [13].
*   **Speak God's Word** The primary way to release or turn your faith loose is by speaking [3][4]. If you believe, you will say what you believe [2]. Dad teaches that you will experience abundance to the degree that you give voice to God's word [4]. He encourages us to speak God's word even before we act, letting all our actions be on the basis of what we have spoken [4]. This includes declaring specific faith confessions, especially when facing challenges like sickness, believing that speaking these potent words causes change and transformation [12].
*   **Act on God's Word** Faith involves both believing and acting on the word of God [3][16]. Sarah, for example, received strength to conceive because she judged God faithful and acted on His promise [3]. At salvation, we believe in our hearts and act by confessing Jesus as Lord [3]. Dad warns against using scripture to counter God's direct instructions, as true faith means doing what God says, regardless of how it might look [15].
*   **Faith is a Gift and an Eternal Possession** Our Senior Pastor explains that the faith of God is a gift, received through hearing and believing God's word (Romans 10:17) [6]. Dad adds that faith is an eternal possession given to us, and it is the way the "God kind" expresses life; there is no other way to express eternal life than by faith [17].

Our Senior Pastor reminds us that being a believer means we have the capacity to believe God, so we should use that capacity and not be doubters [1]. She stresses that the using of faith is individual and personal; merely being around faith or hearing a confession chorused does not affect you unless you put the word in your own mouth and speak it [5].

In "How to Build Lasting Relationships," Andrew Eluwa shared several other points.

He teaches that you should never turn your life into a "prayer project" where you constantly seek out different apostles or prophets, but rather connect with God yourself [6]. He advises that when people offend you, they sometimes don't even know they have done so [2].

He used the parable of the talents (Matthew 25:14-30) to illustrate that it's a "disaster in faith" to hide your gift in church, as the natural tendency is to lose what is not used [11]. Eluwa also highlighted that if you cannot genuinely celebrate others' achievements and be happy for them, people will run away from you, and it's easy to detect this [17]. He cited Judges 7, noting God's method of reducing Gideon's army to illustrate that some people are only with you as long as there's no personal discomfort [5][9][10].

*   In "Arise Early and Be on Your Way 3," Dad explains that as a believer, you have a divine obligation to vote in elections, and if you don't vote, you have no right to complain or pray about the outcome [2]. He stresses the importance of growing in political consciousness and not voting based on excitement or unnecessary sentiments like gender, tribe, or religion, but rather on who can get the job done [1][2]. He also advises practicing delayed spending to allow time for thought before making financial decisions, as many people don't think much about their financial choices [10].

In **Vision Sunday 2026**, Dad points out that your cash balance is not the real status of your finances; rather, it's how you handle your money that determines its health. Your financial status is the health of your finances, determined by how you handle money right now [2].

If something unexpected happens, like losing a parent who was saving for your education, it's important to remember that God is your source, not the person or the money they promised [3].

In **HCM 2025**, Dad shares that he and our Senior Pastor save a percentage of their income for their children's future education, emphasizing that saving for children is an investment and a demonstration of financial discipline that they can learn [4]. In **Honour to Whom It Is Due Part IV**, Dad discusses financial maturity, highlighting that the ability to save money is a major mark of it. In **New Creation Realities**, Dad explains that money issues can break marriages and scatter families. In **A Willing Heart - Giving Series Part 4**, Dad clarifies that it's not bad to be rich, as God has no problem with His children being rich. What God is against is covetousness (Hebrews 13:5), which can affect both the rich and the poor [15].

He encourages letting God's word, not money, control your life and choices [14].

In **No One Is Exempted - Giving Series Part 2**, Dad encourages single ladies to ask potential partners if they save, as discipline with money gives a woman a sense of security in a relationship. He clarifies that this is not materialism, but about good management of money [18].

Discipleship is crucial because it helps believers transition from merely knowing about new creation realities to actively expressing and living in the reality of those truths [3]. It introduces divine order into a believer's life, often requiring them to leave behind old ways or sentiments to embrace God's plan, even when the path isn't fully clear [7]. Discipleship is the "missing link" for those who have received Christ's life but still struggle with old ways of living [15]. It addresses the old life, enabling believers to walk in the newness of life that is theirs in Christ (Romans 6:4, 2 Corinthians 5:17) [17]. The power to say no to sin and change one's thinking, speaking, and actions is already present within a believer, and discipleship helps them activate this dominion over sin (Romans 6:14) [15].

Our Senior Pastor emphasizes several key aspects of discipleship:
*   **A Continuous Learning Process** Christianity is described as scholarly, serious work, not a funfair [3]. Learning continues even after formal education, as discipleship provides the ongoing training and instruction needed to raise a believer to fulfill God's plan [3].
*   **Practical Application for All of Life** Discipleship covers every area of life, teaching how to be an employer, an employee, how to handle business, interact with people, and conduct oneself [4]. It teaches believers to carry out civic duties, be honest, and not cheat or default on debts [16].
*   **Developing Dependence on God** In the kingdom, maturity is marked by increased dependence on God, not independence [2]. Discipleship encourages humility, teachability, and a continuous learning in how to be led by the Spirit, regardless of how long one has been a believer (Psalm 25:9, Proverbs 3:5) [2][12]. It helps believers come under God's divine influence through a closer walk with Him [14].
*   **Building a Prayer Life** Discipleship aids in building a prayer life, which is essential for every believer [8]. The church provides structures, like team leaders, to hold members accountable and ensure consistency in prayer, recognizing that prayer is a spiritual exercise that isn't easily built alone [8].
*   **Fostering Community and Accountability** The local church provides the home and family environment where believers can grow, receive love, care, nourishment, and shelter [1]. Small groups, teams, and sectors within the church create avenues for thorough discipleship, where individuals are known, supported, and gently guided to overcome behavioral and character issues [9]. These structures help members serve and carry out the Great Commission [9].
*   **Teaching Faith** Discipleship teaches faith, enabling believers to understand and apply scriptures like Mark 11:23, which speaks to mountains [6]. Our Senior Pastor highlights that hearing God's Word consistently builds faith for great things, healing, and prosperity (Romans 10:17) [18]. It's about using the faith one already has [18].
*   **Nurturing Relationships** Discipleship teaches the importance of relationships, recognizing that "men are God's methods" for helping us [11]. It cultivates humility and the ability to accept people for who they are, encouraging believers not to burn bridges or discard relationships, as they may be needed in the future, even for generations to come [11].
*   **Living for Posterity** Discipleship instills commitment and teaches believers to live beyond themselves, for posterity and for generations that are coming [11][13]. It helps one remain faithful in commitments, such as marriage or church membership, demonstrating the consistency developed through discipleship [13].
*   **Faithfulness in Passing On Truth** A faithful discipler passes down exactly what they have been taught, communicating the truth of God's Word as they received it, not personal opinions (2 Timothy 2:1-2) [12].

Dad teaches that while the church uses the term "partnership offering" in the New Testament context, he is not against tithing [3][6]. He emphasizes that the primary place of a believer's generosity to the kingdom of God is their local church [3].

Here's what Dad teaches about tithing and giving:
*   **Partnership Offering** In Heritage of Faith Church, the term used is "partnership offering," which is a portion of what God has prospered you with, set aside to support the work of the local church [3]. This is considered the New Testament teaching for giving [3].
*   **Comparison to Old Testament Tithing** Dad encourages believers not to give less than 10% (a tithe of income), because even those in the Old Testament, who did not have the Holy Ghost, gave 10% [3][6]. For New Testament believers in Christ, at least 10% is basic, and one should consider doing even more [6].
*   **Free Will Giving** Giving in the New Testament is an act of free will. While a tithe is encouraged, the percentage is a choice you make, and it can even be less than 10%, though Dad advises against it given the Old Testament example [6]. God does not force anything on anyone [6].
*   **Commitment and the Heart** Giving demonstrates the state of your heart and commitment to God's work, the spread of the gospel, and your purpose in Christ Jesus [9][11]. Where your treasure is, there your heart will be also (Luke 12:34) [11]. Dad recounts the story of Abraham being asked to sacrifice Isaac, noting that God was after Abraham's heart, not just his son [9].
*   **Generosity from God** God increases His children through their giving, a principle that gives God permission to turn insufficiency into more than enough [2]. Generosity is not selective; truly generous people are generous everywhere, not just in church [16].
*   **Giving to Support the Gospel** The partnership offering supports the gospel of Jesus Christ, allowing it to spread [1]. It is one of the ways you show commitment as a church member [1].
*   **Giving Profile** Every year, you should talk to God about what your giving profile (offering, partnership offering, special offerings) should be, as instructed by God, not pressured by man [14][15][18].
*   **God's Valuation of Giving** God values offerings not by the amount given, but by what is left after the person gave [12]. The widow's mite, though seemingly worthless, was considered bigger than everyone else's offering because it was all she had [12].
*   **Giving to Associate Ministers** There is a separate account for giving to appreciate the men and women who serve as associate ministers. Dad notes that gifts given into this account are administered to the associates based on their work and dedication, ensuring nobody is rewarded beyond their dedication [7][17].
*   **Arms Giving vs. Tithing** Giving to beggars on the street is called "arms giving" and God honors it, but it is distinct from tithe or partnership giving to support the gospel [1].

Dad teaches that living by faith is a command from God, not a suggestion, and that faith is never passive [10]. It is an active choice and a decision to walk by faith and put our trust in God [3][5]. Every step a believer takes is meant to be a step of faith [1][8].

Here are some key aspects of what Dad teaches about faith:
*   **Faith vs. Mental Assent** Dad distinguishes between true faith and mental assent. Mental assent may look, talk, and even sometimes behave like faith, but it will not act on God's Word, especially when challenges arise [2]. Mental assent often stems from a lack of attention, where a person's focus is on their needs and problems rather than on God's Word [2][13]. In contrast, true faith is characterized by action on God's Word [2].
*   **Knowledge of God's Will** Faith is not merely knowing God's ability; it is knowing His will—what He is willing and wants to do [4]. Dad emphasizes, "Whatever it is that God can do, he will do it for me" [4]. This persuasion that God *will* act is what constitutes faith [4].
*   **The Spirit of Faith** We have the same spirit of faith, and God gives us faith [7]. As believers, we should only seek to have the things God gives and reject what He didn't give, such as fear. Instead, we should live by faith, talk by faith, and walk by faith [7]. We walk by faith and not by sight, meaning not by our natural senses, because anything beneath God's glory is depraved [7] (2 Corinthians 5:7, Romans 3:23).
*   **Personal Persuasion** While it is good to be in the company of believers, Dad stresses the importance of individual persuasion. If what one calls faith is just communal agreement, it is not true faith. Personal persuasion leads to knowing whom you have believed and being fully persuaded, like Paul, even in the face of suffering [6] (2 Timothy 1:12). Our Senior Pastor adds that we trust God because we see Him in His Word and witness the manifestations of His Word in our lives [16].
*   **Trusting God Alone** Dad teaches that faith means trusting God with our entire lives, not trusting in man, ourselves, our bosses, or our investments [17]. Our trust in God determines what good we see coming our way [17] (Jeremiah 17:5-6, Job 22:21).
*   **Showtime** When we consistently engage in spiritual practices like reading the Bible, praying, confessing God's Word in faith, and sitting under the ministration of God's Word, it is "showtime." Everything we are trusting God for—sound health, healing, wholeness, fruit of the womb, character change, or overcoming sinful habits—will manifest and dematerialize what we don't want to see [12].
